label: Thomistic charity highest-good and role-indexed hierarchy test (#1747/#1460)
summary: Tested a differentiated moral hierarchy on a fixed equal-need child/virtuous-stranger help case, expressly conditional on h being the child's parent and (for Aquinas ST II-II q26 aa1,6,7,9) h acting under theological charity. q26 positively distinguishes object-directed goodness and charity's relational intensity/care, with an ultimate Good as final-end reference; it does not provide a universal natural-law action calculator or divine cognition from human order. A JavaScript finite scope check held the two typed strict preference relations separate (each irreflexive, asymmetric, transitive), then found the untyped union non-asymmetric and non-transitive because s>c under the first relation and c>s under the second. Three structural source profiles retained identical rankings and facts while varying HasIntellect(n) and actual end-adoption, illustrating weak-schema non-entailment; this is not a model of full Thomistic charity or a defeat of a strong authored-source premise. Positive Foot/natural-goodness and Wielenberg/robust-norm completions can likewise give relationship-sensitive reasons; their concrete care/duty tie-breakers need content warrant. The Thomistic account has conditional unifying explanatory reach, but the fixed hierarchy alone does not selectively establish same-source intellect, capacity will or actual willing. Novelty is a concrete q26 instantiation of #1460's existing two-axis plan, no new Lean theorem or philosophical rival defeat. Source locator: https://www.newadvent.org/summa/3026.htm; connected assessment: docs/notes/moral-governance-intellect-will.md. A distinct ST I-II q94 a2/a4 source pass identifies offspring education as a natural-law good under ordinary human practical reason, without theological Charity(h). This is a weaker support option only for that content step, not for the entire q26 hierarchy or the fixed equal-need rescue priority: education-to-selected-aid applicability, agent-indexed duty and priority remain open. It supplies no inference to intellect/will of the necessary source.
blocker: ST I-II q94 supports the offspring-education good without charity; extending it to actual parent rescue aid, categorical duty and conflict ranking still needs a reason/justice and application bridge. The entire q26 charity hierarchy still cannot be generalized to all natural-law duties without an additional interpretation bridge. To prove source intellect/will, identify the highest final Good with the actual necessary root n and justify that n itself understands, institutes and adopts the morally authoritative role-sensitive ends, rather than merely causing agents who reason about them. Distinguish finite control from actual God-model. #1460 owns a full formal priority/ranking argument; no premise/frontier status changes.
